title: An Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array Survey of Chemistry in Disks around M4-M5 Stars
question: What is the chemistry of protoplanetary disks around low-mass M4-M5 stars at 10-100 AU scales, and how does it compare to disks around solar-type stars?

data.sensitivity: 0.03-0.09 mJy beam^-1 (continuum rms); 1.6-4.2 mJy beam^-1 (line channel rms)

what.value: Stellar spectral types, ages, luminosities, masses, effective temperatures, and literature distances for the 5 target disks

evidence.quote: The stellar ages ($t_*$), stellar luminosities ($L_*$), stellar masses ($M_*$), and stellar effective temperatures ($T_\mathrm{eff}$) were taken from the literature, where they were derived from continuum photometry, spectral energy distribution (SED) fits, scaling relations, and/or stellar evolutionary models.

recipe.goal: Estimate disk centers and extract line/continuum emission with Keplerian masks
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussians to the dust continuum to find disk centers; apply Keplerian masks across emission velocity channels to extract spectra, moment 0 maps, radial profiles, and integrated fluxes; estimate uncertainties via 1000 random/bootstrapped samples.
key_parameters: Keplerian mask parameters: V_0 = 0.22-0.25 km/s, R_0 = 100 AU, q = 0.3, and disk-specific theta_alpha, theta_beta, V_LSR, and mask extents (Table 6)
Detection criteria: >= 3 sigma in velocity-integrated map and peak >= 3 sigma in at least 3 channels within Keplerian mask
assumptions: Combined thermal and turbulent line width follows power law Delta V ~ V_0 (R_0/100)^q
Literature distances in parentheses (140 pc for Taurus, 160 pc for Chamaeleon I, 150 pc for Lupus)

recipe.goal: Compare relative line fluxes and compute correlation coefficients across M4-M5 and solar-type/Herbig Ae disks
recipe.method: Normalize integrated line fluxes to 140 pc, compute Spearman and Pearson correlation coefficients in log-log space for molecule pairs, and analyze flux ratios vs stellar mass and radius.
assumptions: H2CO 3_03-2_02 and 4_04-3_03 line fluxes from the literature have similar flux behaviors and can be combined

recipe.goal: Fit pixel-by-pixel hyperfine spectra of C2H and HCN in J1100-7619 to derive radial profiles of T_ex, tau, and N_tot
recipe.method: Reimage C2H and HCN in J1100-7619 at 0.14 km/s resolution; fit 4-parameter LTE hyperfine model per pixel using MCMC; compute T_ex, tau, and N_tot per pixel; construct weighted radial profiles over valid pixels in deprojected annuli.
key_parameters: Valid pixel criteria: SNR of faintest resolved hyperfine component >= 3, relative parameter errors <= 0.20, flux difference f_50 <= 0.20
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), identical line width for each hyperfine component, homogeneous excitation conditions along line of sight, filling factor f = 1

recipe.goal: Estimate disk-averaged column densities and column density ratios for C2H, HCN, and DCN across the sample
recipe.method: Extract emission within the 1-sigma radial profile extent; solve a linear system of equations (Mx = b) to decompose blended hyperfine flux into individual component fluxes for assumed T_ex and tau ranges; compute disk-averaged N_tot.
key_parameters: Emission extent defined where radial profile decreases to 1 sigma
assumptions: T_ex = 10-30 K (median 20 K) for C2H, HCN, and DCN; tau = 1-5 (median 2) for C2H; tau = 4-12 (median 8) for HCN; DCN is optically thin

answer_key.quantity: Disk-averaged median C2H column density across M4-M5 sample

evidence.quote: The median C$_2$H column density estimates are (5-10)$\times 10^{13}$ cm$^{-2}$ across the sample. Changing the excitation temperature and opacity result in factors of 2-4 higher or lower estimates of the column density.

answer_key.quantity: Disk-averaged median HCN column density across M4-M5 sample

evidence.quote: The median HCN column density estimates span a factor of 3, from (4-12)$\times 10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$. Changes in optical depth from 4 to 12 lead to factors $\lesssim$3 in difference between estimates, while changes in excitation temperature from 10K to 30K lead to factors of $\sim$3-10 (excluding Sz 69).

answer_key.quantity: J1100-7619 disk-averaged median DCN column density

evidence.quote: For the bright and well-resolved disk J1100-7619, DCN is detected, and the estimated column densities (not shown) span $\sim$(4-10)$\times 10^{11}$ cm$^{-2}$ from 10-30K with a median of $\sim$7$\times 10^{11}$ cm$^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: Disk-averaged median C2H/HCN column density ratio across M4-M5 sample

evidence.quote: Median estimates of the ratio range from $\sim$7 for FP Tau to $\sim$11 for J1545-3417.

answer_key.quantity: J1100-7619 disk-averaged median DCN/HCN column density ratio

evidence.quote: This disk has a median DCN/HCN value of $\sim$0.072 and ranges from $\sim$0.04-0.1 across the extremes.

score_reason: Complete and detailed mathematical and procedural description of Keplerian masking (Table 6), hyperfine MCMC fitting (Appendix 8), and column density matrix inversion (Appendix 9), with CASA version, robust parameter, pixel sizes, and velocity channel widths explicitly given. Minor deductions for hand-drawn CLEAN masks, unstated line-free channel ranges, and solint given only as ranges.
rediscovery_reason: Public single-project ALMA dataset (2017.1.01107.S), well-specified imaging and Keplerian mask parameters (Table 6), and explicit numerical answer keys for continuum fluxes (Table 4), line fluxes/radii (Table 5), correlations (Table 7), and column densities.
